reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes BNB flash-loan arbitrage by claiming that a small amount of BNB can produce more than 10 BNB within minutes. It instructs viewers to obtain contract code, connect MetaMask, deploy a contract, send BNB to it, and execute the action, while linking greater deposited liquidity to greater returns. Although the destination, transactions, and losses are unverified, the described promotion, requested BNB transfer, and claimed profit mechanism support the classification.

citations.quote: I've done, you'll see how I used just .3 BNB to gain over 10.7 BNB in just minutes.
Here I'll choose, 0.3 BNB. Set your deposit and then click to confirm.
we are going to execute the flash loan attack.
This will connect your Metamask Browser wallet, if it isn't connected already, so that you can interact with the contract.
Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+ (0.3 up is better as you will get a bigger amount in each swap)

opening.argument: Judge the full explanation, not just its most striking result. The speaker says returns vary with network volume and liquidity and acknowledges that some attempts produce only a small amount. The description also warns that flash-loan exploits have been used to steal funds and discusses failed attempts and changing fees. Those cautions do not prove the method works, but they make a reading of this as an unqualified promise of profit less persuasive. It can instead be read as a risky technical demonstration whose outcome is expressly uncertain.

citations.quote: the return is different every time depending on the network volume and the amount of liquidity you put in.
Sometimes you will get a small amount, while other times you can hit it big like we did here.
flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
because fees may be different from day to day. (1.5+ BNB for each 1000 BNB you are borrowing) Avoid using very low amounts as contract may fail below 0.15 BNB.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening statement correctly identifies a claimed result and a BNB transfer, but it treats that result as though it stands alone. The speaker explicitly says returns differ and can be small; the description even anticipates a failed attempt. Connecting a wallet and funding a contract are consequential steps, yet those steps do not erase the stated uncertainty or establish that the reported return was guaranteed.

citations.quote: the return is different every time depending on the network volume and the amount of liquidity you put in.
Under some very rare cases, the arbitrage might fail

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Variable returns are still presented as returns from funding and executing this contract. The speaker links higher liquidity to higher return on investment, while the description tells viewers to send BNB and suggests sending more if the first amount does not work. Acknowledging fees or occasional failure does not neutralize that deposit-driven profit pitch.

opening.argument: This is structured around operating development tools: creating a Solidity file, selecting a matching compiler, deploying through Remix and interacting with the resulting contract. The sampled screens show code and the Remix deployment interface. The speaker walks through an example rather than merely displaying a profit claim. The claimed outcome deserves scrutiny, but a technical walkthrough with visible development steps can reasonably be assessed as a demonstration, not solely as a solicitation.

citations.quote: Name the file something like FlashLoan.sol Now you want to paste in the smart contract code into this new file
pick the compiler that matches the top of the code. Then go down and click compile.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening emphasizes the wallet connection, BNB transfer and asserted gain, all of which matter. But it omits how much of the presentation is devoted to making and deploying a contract. The speaker explains that the wallet connection enables interaction with that contract; the deployment screen is shown. Those details support an instructional reading even though they cannot verify the claimed result.

citations.quote: This will connect your Metamask Browser wallet, if it isn't connected already, so that you can interact with the contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is precisely how viewers are led to fund the proposed profit mechanism. After deployment, the speaker directs them to send BNB to the contract and execute its action, then attributes a large gain to the process. Showing an IDE does not turn a funded-contract return pitch into neutral programming instruction.

citations.quote: Go to your Wallet and click SEND. Copy and paste the new contract code here.
click the red button to execute your flash loan
I used just .3 BNB to gain over 10.7 BNB in just minutes.

opening.argument: The instructions describe using a browser wallet with a newly deployed contract, including ordinary transaction confirmations and gas fees. They do not, on their face, establish who controls the contract or where its funds ultimately go. The description even tells the viewer to transfer BNB out to another wallet when finished. The large return claim is a serious reason for skepticism, but the supplied presentation does not independently establish diversion of funds, a credential request, or a verified loss. The narrower reading is a proposed contract-based activity whose claimed results remain unverified.

citations.quote: Once you click Transact, you'll get a pop-up asking for the Gas Fees to create your new token contract. Confirm in your wallet
Copy and paste the new contract code here. Then choose the amount of liquidity you want to place.
Make sure to transfer your BNB out to another wallet when you're done.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening itself notes that the destination, transactions and losses are unverified. A direction to send BNB to a deployed contract shows a funding step, but does not by itself show who receives the funds or whether the asserted outcome occurred. That evidentiary limit matters when distinguishing a questionable contract workflow from an established scheme to take viewers' money.

citations.quote: Copy the address of the newly deployed contract. 17. Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap
After your network confirmation it may take a few minutes to receive the return if everything was done correctly.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A verified theft or loss is not needed to assess what the video promotes. It supplies external contract code, directs viewers to fund the deployed contract, and explicitly connects a larger deposit with a larger return. The suggestion to transfer funds out afterward does not establish that viewers can do so, and the missing independent verification does not remove the funded-return solicitation.
